newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
LALOO LOYALISTS SEEK GUJARAL'S INTERVENTION

Supporters of Bihar state Chief Minister Laloo Yadav sought the intervention of Prime Minister I.K. Gujral to find a solution to the crisis in the Janata Dal party. They said they would go ahead with the plan to conduct a separate poll to elect a new party president. The prime minister is not very hopeful of a compromise between Laloo Yadav and his opponent, Sharad Yadav. While the joint director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) said the CBI would soon seek government permission to prosecute Laloo Yadav and the other accused in another case related to the fodder case.
The Economic Times
QUICK NOD FOR FAST-TRACK PROJECTS

The Power Ministry plans to push through eight fast-track power projects and take steps to privatise power distribution whereever possible as part of an effort to increase supply of power in the short run. It will also fix a schedule for plants managed by the state electricity boards to improve the plant load factor. The power minister said renovation of plants alone would generate an extra 3,500 to 4,000 megawatts of power. Schedules and responsibilities were fixed for clearing the eight fast-track projects. At least three of these projects are awaiting counter guarantee from the Centre.
CONSULTANTS FOR BIG CORE PROJECTS PLANNED

Financial institutions are considering appointing independent consultants for large infrastructure projects which they finance. As a beginning they may bring in an international consultant o monitor the setting up of a 58.15 billion-rupee refinery project of the Essar Oil. This may lead to the appointment of consultants to projects facing time and cost overruns. The plan to appoint a consultant for the Essar Oil project is aimed at ensuring the proper use of funds and to see that funds are not diverted to other projects.
GOVERNMENT TO PUMP IN 16 BLN IN TO INDIAN BANK

The government is planning to infuse 16 billion rupee as capital into the Indian Bank to restore its profit net worth. The money will be issued as recapitalisation bonds. Issuing such bonds through a double-book entry is an accepted practice in a number of developing countries. Finance Ministry officials said the package was nearly finalised. It will help the Madras-based Indian Bank to begin afresh after losing over 10 billion rupees from its net worth during 1995/96 (April-March).
Financial Express
REPORT ON MONEY LAUNDERING BILL ON MONDAY

An inter-ministerial group may submit on Monday its report on the Money Laundering Bill. The bill will complement the proposed Foreign Exchange Management Act. It will primarily track criminal activities on the basis of money squandered. The representatives of the Enforcement Directorate are likely to write a descending note while submitting the report. The directorate fears it will loss its power to investigate economic offences. But it is believed that the group has agreed that bank accounts worth more than 10 million rupees should be probed.
Business Standard
EXPORTS UP BY 8PCT IN MAY

Exports grew by eight percent in May. The Commerce Ministry is expected to fix $40 billion as the official export target for 1997/98 (April-March), implying an export growth rate of 20 percent. The export target for 1996/97 was $38 billion but actual exports were $33 billion. Exporters have demanded concessions including a cut by one percent in post-shipment credit interest rates and removal of the 20 percent minimum export growth limit expected from trading houses.
COMPUTER PRICES TO FALL

The prices of computers and several related items will drop significantly from Tuesday when the Information Technology Agreement (ITA) comes into effect. Under the ITA India will cut import duties on 207 items from July 1, 1997. But the new tariff will take effect from March 1 as the Indian annual Financial Bill is usually presented in parliament on the last day of February. The duties will be brought down to 10 levels. This varies between 12 percent and 100 percent. The duty on optical fibre cables will drop to 42 percent this July from 110 percent. This will benefit private telecommunication service operators. The duty on populated printed circuit boards will be cut down to 32 percent this July and would be phased out by the year 2000.
SOFTWARE MAJORS ASKED TO OFFER RISK COVER

Financial institutions and banks asked software majors to offer risk cover to facilitate credit flow to smaller software developers in line with the trends in the Silicon Valley in the United States. A few of the major units are planning to put this proposal before the National Association of Software and Service Companies.
The Observer
STANDARD & POORS TO REVISE RATING ON INDIA

International credit rating agency Standard and Poors will soon revise its rating of the Indian economy. Representatives of the agency will meet Finance Ministry officials on Monday to discuss the recent performance of Indian economy and the policy initiatives taken for the coming months. The representatives will also hold meetings with other ministries, industrialists, investment agencies, leading economists and analysts. The agency's rating will be critical in influencing investment inflows into India.
40 PCT FOREIGN EQUITY IN DOMESTIC AIRLIINES

The government may allow 40 percent foreign equity in domestic airlines. The draft of the new aviation policy says domestic operators will be allowed a foreign equity of up to 40 percent irrespective of the equity source. The existing air service agreements will be amended to allow multiple designation. If possible at least dual designation for more Indian operators to fly to international destinations will be allowed. The new draft policy says the chairman, the managing director or the chief executive officer and two thirds of the directors in the board such an airline should be Indians including non-resident Indians.
PLAN TO CAP INFRASTRUCTURAL SNAGS

The government is trying to evolve a multi-pronged strategy to overcome infrastructure snags and their adverse fallout on industrial growth. Steps will be taken to increase the quantum and quantity of public sector investment in key infrastructure sectors. The Finance Ministry will discuss plans to attract private investments in infrastructure projects by eliminating the institutional hurdles, particularly those relating to mobilising long-term finance. The ministry estimates India needs $400 billion investment in the infrastructure in the next 10 years. Out of this $80 billion will be used to bridge the shortfalls in the power sector.
NATIONAL DEPOSITORY TO ALLOW MUTUAL FUNDS ENTRY

The National Securities Depository decided to allow mutual funds to join it. This will allow investors to hold mutual fund units in the book-entry form and enable their fast transfer. It will also eliminate risks of transfer delays and other associated risks. So far only shares and debt instruments have been allowed into the depository. Industry sources said the Morgan Stanley Growth Fund had already approached the National Securities Depository to place their units as an eligible security. Many other leading mutual fund players are planning to do the same.
